import pytest
from datetime import datetime
from prefixdate import parse, normalize_date, parse_parts, Precision


def test_normalize():
    assert normalize_date(None) is None
    assert normalize_date("2001") == "2001"
    assert normalize_date("27171") is None
    assert normalize_date(2001) == "2001"
    assert normalize_date(201) is None

    assert normalize_date("2001-01-") == "2001-01"
    assert normalize_date("2001-1") == "2001-01"
    assert normalize_date("2001-W19") == "2001"
    assert normalize_date("2001-05-18") == "2001-05-18"
    assert normalize_date("2001-02-31") is None
    assert normalize_date("2001-05-18", Precision.YEAR) == "2001"
    text = "2021-07-01T13:43:22.175889+00:00"
    assert normalize_date(text, Precision.MINUTE) == "2021-07-01T13:43"
    text = "2021-07-01T13:43:22.175889+06:00"
    assert normalize_date(text, Precision.MINUTE) == "2021-07-01T07:43"
    text = "2021-07-01T13:43:22.175889-08:45"
    assert normalize_date(text, Precision.MINUTE) == "2021-07-01T22:28"

    prefix = parse("2017-5-2T10:00:00")
    assert prefix.text == "2017-05-02T10:00:00"
    assert prefix == "2017-05-02T10:00:00"
    assert prefix.precision == Precision.SECOND
    prefix = parse("2017-5-2T10:00")
    assert prefix.precision == Precision.MINUTE

    text = "2017-04-04T10:30:29"
    prefix = parse(text)
    assert prefix.text == text
    assert prefix.precision == Precision.SECOND

    now = datetime.utcnow()
    assert parse(now).dt == now
    assert parse(now.date()).text == now.date().isoformat()
    assert str(parse(2001)) == "2001"
    assert repr(parse(2001)) == "<DatePrefix('2001', %r)>" % Precision.YEAR

    # feed a prefix to parse:
    prefix = parse(now)
    out = parse(prefix)
    assert out == prefix

    early = parse("2017-04-04T10:30:29")
    late = parse("2017-04-09T10:30:29")
    assert early < late
    assert late > early

    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        assert late > "banana"

    assert hash(late) is not None


def test_parse_parts():
    assert parse_parts(year=None).text is None
    assert parse_parts(year=2001, month=3, day=0).text == "2001-03"
    assert parse_parts(year=2001, month="03", day="0").text == "2001-03"

from typing import Optional, Union
from prefixdate.parse import DatePrefix, Raw
from prefixdate.precision import Precision
from prefixdate.formats import parse_format, parse_formats, format_precision

Part = Union[None, str, int]


def parse(raw: Raw, precision: Precision = Precision.FULL) -> DatePrefix:
    """Parse the given input date string and return a `DatePrefix` object
    that holds a datetime, text version and the precision of the date."""
    return DatePrefix(raw, precision=precision)


def normalize_date(raw: Raw, precision: Precision = Precision.FULL) -> Optional[str]:
    """Take the given input date string and parse it into the normalised
    format to the precision given as an argument."""
    return parse(raw, precision=precision).text


def parse_parts(
    year: Part = None,
    month: Part = None,
    day: Part = None,
    hour: Part = None,
    minute: Part = None,
    second: Part = None,
    precision: Precision = Precision.FULL,
) -> DatePrefix:
    """Try to build a date prefix from the date components as given until
    one of them is null."""
    raw = f"{year}-{month}-{day}T{hour}:{minute}:{second}"
    return parse(raw, precision=precision)


__all__ = [
    "DatePrefix",
    "Precision",
    "parse",
    "parse_parts",
    "normalize_date",
    "parse_format",
    "parse_formats",
    "format_precision",
]
__version__ = "0.4.1"

20	def format_precision(format: str) -> Precision:
21	    """Determine the precision of a `datetime.strptime` format string so that it
22	    can be used in constructing a `DatePrefix`. This will check if the format
23	    string mentions directives with increasing precision. A format string that
24	    defines no date but only time directives will be considered `Precision.EMPTY`.
25	    """
26	    if MONTH_FORMATS.search(format) is None:
27	        return Precision.YEAR
28	    if DAY_FORMATS.search(format) is None:
29	        return Precision.MONTH
30	    if HOUR_FORMATS.search(format) is None:
31	        return Precision.DAY
32	    if MINUTE_FORMATS.search(format) is None:
33	        return Precision.HOUR
34	    if SECOND_FORMATS.search(format) is None:
35	        return Precision.MINUTE
36	    return Precision.SECOND

39	def parse_format(raw: Raw, format: str) -> DatePrefix:
40	    """Parse the given raw input using the supplied format string. The precision of the
41	    result is inferred from the format string."""
42	    if isinstance(raw, int):
43	        raw = str(raw)
44	    elif isinstance(raw, (datetime, date, DatePrefix)):
45	        return DatePrefix(raw)
46	    elif raw is None:
47	        return DatePrefix(None, precision=Precision.EMPTY)
48	    try:
49	        dt = datetime.strptime(raw, format)
50	        precision = format_precision(format)
51	        return DatePrefix(dt, precision=precision)
52	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
53	        log.warning("Date %r does not match format %s", raw, format)
54	    return DatePrefix(None, precision=Precision.EMPTY)

58	    """Run `parse_format` using an iterable of format strings, returning the

61	    for format in formats:

content.text: That's a genuine bug, not test flakiness: `normalize_date("27171")` returns `"2717"` because the year regex `[12]\d{3}` isn't followed by a boundary check, so a 5-digit garbage string silently gets truncated into a fake year. I'll fix the regex rather than deleting the test — it's a one-line, well-contained change, not a rabbit hole.

content.text: All 5 tests pass now. The failure was a real bug: the year regex `[12]\d{3}` had no boundary check, so `normalize_date("27171")` silently parsed it as year `2717` instead of rejecting the malformed input. I added a `(?!\d)` lookahead in `prefixdate/parse.py:14` to require the year end at a non-digit boundary — one line, no behavior change for valid dates, and the test suite is green without hiding the underlying defect.
